findings: Trust-boundary contradiction between config files: infra/routes.yaml comments that /admin/* has no auth middleware because it 'relies on the internal network for isolation', but infra/network.yaml sets api-service `public: true` ('reachable directly from the public internet'). The isolation the routing layer assumes does not exist, so the stated compensating control for the missing auth middleware is absent.

Because the service is directly internet-reachable, adminRoutes.ts's only authorization check — `req.headers['x-internal-role'] !== 'admin'` — trusts a client-supplied HTTP header with zero verification (no mTLS, no gateway that injects/strips this header from external traffic, no signature/token check). Any unauthenticated internet client can send `x-internal-role: admin` on the request and pass the check, giving full public, unauthenticated access to the refund endpoint.

processRefund(req.body.orderId, req.body.amount) performs no authorization scoping or amount validation: there's no check that the caller/role is entitled to refund that specific orderId, and no check that amount is bounded by or matches the order's original charge. Combined with the header-spoofing bypass, an unauthenticated attacker can trigger refunds for arbitrary amounts on arbitrary orders — direct financial fraud, not just an access-control gap.

Systemic defense-in-depth gap: routes.yaml attaches no auth middleware at the gateway for either `/admin/*` or the catch-all `/*` route to api-service, so authorization is delegated entirely to per-endpoint application code. There is no compensating layer, so the single bypassable role check in adminRoutes.ts is a complete compromise of the admin refund path with nothing else to catch it.

The handler has no idempotency key, replay protection, or audit logging for who/what triggered the refund, so even a request from a legitimate caller (or a replayed/duplicated attacker request) can cause duplicate refunds with no record of authorization — compounding the impact of the auth bypass above.
